subject.title: Cron allows invalid Feishu announce jobs without delivery.to, causing runtime delivery failure

question: Should maintainers refresh/adopt one of the two open fork PRs that close this issue, or close both and allow a narrow replacement fix?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but duplicate open fix candidates already exist and are conflicting, so a maintainer should choose the landing path before ClawSweeper queues new work.

options.title: Refresh or adopt a fork PR
options.body: Review the two open fork PRs and update the cleaner candidate into a focused gateway/service validation fix with regression coverage.

options.title: Close both and replace
options.body: Close the conflicting fork PRs, then queue a new narrow fix PR that preserves the issue evidence and credits the prior attempts.

options.title: Defer broader UX work
options.body: Keep this issue focused on create-time validation and file a separate follow-up for cron audit and diagnostic wording if desired.

recommendation.title: Refresh or adopt a fork PR
recommendation.body: Review the two open fork PRs and update the cleaner candidate into a focused gateway/service validation fix with regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest recent owner signal for the current cron gateway/service validation surface.
